scope: Independent Runtime review assertions on the evolving v0.7 candidate, separate from process-restart qualification and the full regression.

cases.name: Exhausted shared in-memory root must not count an undispatched action
cases.green: 0 dispatches, no unknown effects, original root usage retained.

cases.name: Exhausted real SQLite root reservation
cases.green: Only the first handler dispatch and durable root unit are counted.

cases.name: Recovery uses persisted effective arguments
cases.red: Passed before this review round: reconciliation observed effective arguments and did not call the original execute handler.

cases.name: Terminal outcome consistency
cases.red: A synthetic SQLite mutation changed outcome.answer independently from the settled Runtime state and was returned as completed.
cases.green: The contradictory stored outcome is refused rather than returned as a second truth.

cases.name: Original assistant/tool call pairing
cases.red: A synthetic SQLite mutation changed tool.callId and the next Gateway request still ran to completion.
cases.green: The malformed executable history is refused before any additional Gateway call.

cases.name: Cancellation retains already committed report
cases.red: Actual first report receipt existed; cancelled readback returned no receipt.
cases.green: Cancelled readback retains the same known report receipt, validates its bytes, and makes no additional Gateway request.

cases.name: Duplicate proposed IDs in a pending suffix
cases.red: A corrupted active proposal with duplicate call IDs in the not-yet-consumed suffix was accepted and the Run completed.
cases.green: The invalid proposal is refused before another model request or tool reservation.

cases.name: Already consumed group with a rewound cursor
cases.red: A corrupted active checkpoint rewound the cursor to an already consumed call and the Run completed after replay.
cases.green: Cursor must agree with the actual paired history; refusal preserves the original model and tool counts.

cases.name: Recovered source payload remains bound to its original Host record
cases.red: Host snapshot and original source records still reopened successfully. Only the historical tool payload text and its matching hash were changed in synthetic SQLite. Resume made a third Gateway request instead of refusing at the two original requests.
cases.green: The self-consistent but non-original historical source payload is rejected before any additional Gateway request.

cases.name: Recovered method payload remains bound to its acquired method snapshot
cases.red: Host.methods remained original and valid. Only historical tool payload text, its matching hash and matching version were changed in synthetic SQLite. Resume made a third Gateway request.
cases.green: The altered method payload is rejected before another Gateway request; correct Host.methods alone no longer legitimizes a contradictory model input.

boundaries: Two tests intentionally alter only isolated synthetic SQLite snapshots to test corrupt-state handling; no existing or production database is opened.
The reconciliation test verifies the selected adapter call boundary only; it is not by itself a process-restart demonstration.
The cancellation test reopens the same real SQLite database in-process. The separate durable-runtime process suite is required to establish actual kill/new-process recovery.
Recorded hashes are observed after each command on a shared evolving candidate, not a claim of an immutable complete dependency closure. Final qualification must pin and regress the full candidate.
Raw test output stays ignored under test-output; this file contains only sanitized authored observations.
